subsystems.name: Foundation model
subsystems.role: provides the language understanding and reasoning that drives the agent.

subsystems.name: Agent loop
subsystems.role: plans and acts step by step, deciding what to do next.

subsystems.name: Tool layer
subsystems.role: lets the agent affect real systems rather than just produce text.

subsystems.name: Memory
subsystems.role: remembers past interactions and retrieves relevant knowledge.

subsystems.name: Orchestration
subsystems.role: coordinates multiple steps or multiple agents working together.

subsystems.name: Guardrails and evaluation
subsystems.role: keeps actions safe, correct and within limits.

buildSteps.title: Define the workflow
buildSteps.detail: Break a business process into discrete steps, decide which can be automated, and set success metrics.

buildSteps.title: Choose a base model
buildSteps.detail: Select a large language model with strong reasoning and tool-use ability, then adapt it by prompting or fine-tuning.

buildSteps.title: Expose tools
buildSteps.detail: Wrap each software system (CRM, email, database) as a function the agent can call, with clear inputs and outputs.

buildSteps.title: Implement the agent loop
buildSteps.detail: Build a ReAct-style cycle: the model reasons about the next step, calls a tool, observes the result, and repeats until the task is done.

buildSteps.title: Add memory
buildSteps.detail: Store past interactions and documents in a vector database so the agent can retrieve relevant context instead of relying only on the prompt.

buildSteps.title: Insert guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Limit permissions, require human approval for sensitive actions, and log every decision for audit.

buildSteps.title: Test in simulation
buildSteps.detail: Run the agent on historical cases and in shadow mode alongside humans, comparing its output to what people did.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with oversight
buildSteps.detail: Start with a human reviewing each completed task, then gradually widen autonomy as reliability is proven.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Track failures, retrain or re-prompt, and expand the agent's scope as the toolset and confidence grow.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with chain-of-thought reasoning
prerequisites.why: the agent needs to decompose tasks and explain its steps.
the agent must reliably invoke external software, not just generate text.
long-term memory depends on storing and fetching relevant context quickly.
measuring whether an agent completed a real task correctly is still an open problem.
agents can forget, hallucinate or contradict earlier decisions over long workflows.
the agent can only act where software exposes a programmable interface.

pathway.milestone: copilots that assist with single steps, such as drafting an email or writing code
pathway.unlocks: productivity gains where a human remains in the loop.

pathway.milestone: agents that complete well-scoped multi-step tasks in one domain, like reconciling invoices
pathway.unlocks: automation of routine back-office work with human review.

pathway.milestone: multi-agent systems that run entire processes end to end
pathway.unlocks: faster cycle times and fewer handoffs between people.

pathway.milestone: agents that learn from feedback and improve across domains
pathway.unlocks: broad autonomy, if reliability, safety and accountability are solved.
